QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_18

question.text: Option buyers in commodity derivatives are charged:

answer.text: Only the premium during normal pre-expiry option buying — with exceptions for delivery-period margin on Options on Goods and devolvement margin on Options on Futures
Initial margin, ELM, and MTM like futures traders at all times
Half the margin of futures traders

explanation.text: The Logic: Ordinarily, an option buyer in commodity derivatives pays only the premium and is not subjected to initial margin, ELM or MTM during the normal pre-expiry life of the option. However, for Options on Goods, delivery-period margin can apply to buyers (and sellers) of ITM/CTM or expected ITM/CTM positions close to expiry, and for Options on Futures, devolvement margin can be charged on both sides as the option moves toward devolvement into a futures position. The Trap: Saying "no other margin is applicable" without qualification overlooks the late-cycle delivery-period and devolvement-stage charges that can fall on option buyers in commodity options. Note: The "buyer pays only premium" simplification is accurate for pre-expiry positioning but should be qualified when discussing the last few days before expiry or devolvement.
